cli_tool.authentication: API key generated via CLI login or web signup

web_app.backend_api: Same as CLI — calls DeepSeek API via your own proxy (for rate limiting, billing)

web_users.primary_value: higher willingness to pay, less churn

revenue_comparison.conclusion: Web users generate 2-3x more revenue per user, but CLI users drive acquisition. For a bootstrapped system, web revenue dominates after 6 months.

web_dashboard_feasibility.answer: Yes, a static HTML/JS page can call your API directly. Use client-side API keys with CORS restrictions and rate limiting. For Stripe, use Stripe Checkout (redirect) — no server needed. Example: static site on Vercel with environment variables for API endpoint.

implementation_steps: 1. Set up DeepSeek API account and get API key.
2. Build backend proxy (FastAPI) with user auth, rate limiting, usage logging.
3. Create Stripe product and price IDs.
4. Build CLI tool (Node.js) — use 'commander' for CLI, 'axios' for API calls.
5. Build web app (Next.js static export) — use 'next-auth' for login, Stripe Checkout for payment.
6. Deploy backend to Railway or Fly.io, web to Vercel, CLI to npm.
7. Test end-to-end: CLI free tier -> web upgrade -> usage tracking.
